saints.name: St. Giles
saints.title: Abbot and Hermit
saints.shortBlurb: A hermit of the forests near the Rhône whose solitary holiness drew a monastery and the veneration of all Christendom…
biography: According to his early medieval legend Giles (Aegidius) was born in Greece and came west, settling as a hermit in the wilderness near the mouth of the Rhône in southern France, where a hind is said to have sustained and sheltered him. A Visigothic or Frankish king, discovering him while hunting, endowed a monastery over which Giles ruled as abbot until his death about 710.

The abbey and town of Saint-Gilles grew into a great pilgrimage centre on the road to Compostela. Counted among the Fourteen Holy Helpers, Giles became one of the most popular saints of the Middle Ages, invoked especially by the crippled, lepers, and nursing mothers.
saints.knownFor: His life of hermit solitude and the great pilgrim abbey that bears his name.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 1 September
